source_title: Christopher Lloyd Jokes About Turning 88 in ‘Back to the Future’ Nod (Exclusive) - People.com
source_excerpt:
The Emmy-winning actor celebrated the milestone of his 88th birthday on Oct. 22
Universal/Getty; Rodin Eckenroth/WireImage
Christopher Lloyd discusses his new memoir, In My Own Time , in this week’s issue of PEOPLE
The actor jokes that upon turning 88 this month, he is “going to see some serious [s---],” a reference to his Back to the Future character Doc Brown
Coincidentally, just ahead of the actor’s birthday, Tesla unveiled what appeared to be a flying car reminiscent of his iconic DeLorean in Back to the Future
For Christopher Lloyd , the number 88 has long had special significance: it’s the amount of miles per hour required for the DeLorean’s time travel in 1985’s Back to the Future , his best-known movie.
So the veteran actor approached his recent 88th birthday (on Oct. 22) with some anticipation, he tells PEOPLE in this week’s issue. “I’m glad that I’m still alive,” quips the actor.
In his new memoir In My Own Time (out now), Lloyd paraphrases Dr. Emmett “Doc” Brown, his character in the three beloved Back to the Future movies, talking about hitting 88 miles an hour: “I’m eighty-seven as I write this and will soon hit eighty-eight, which, I am told, is when you’re going to see some serious s---.”
Amblin Entertainment/Universal Pictures/Kobal/Shutterstock
Lisa Lloyd , Christopher’s wife since 2016, “brought to my attention” that another strange coincidence preceded his big milestone by mere days, he says. On Oct. 16, Tesla CEO Elon Musk unveiled a new Roadster that appeared to be able to fly — just like Doc Brown’s plutonium-powered time machine.
“You hit 88 and the world’s first flying car comes out a few days before,” says Lisa, 56. “There you go.”
Her husband, she explains, “isn’t on social media” so missed the internet’s assertion that he should advertise Tesla’s new invention. “I said to Chris, ‘You might not think this, but you’re in the conversation out there on the internet about this because everyone right now is stunned at Elon’s flying car.’”
Jokes Lloyd with a grin: “We’re going to exploit the hell out of that.”
On the actor’s birthday, fans — including Back to the Future costar Michael J. Fox — celebrated the Taxi Emmy winner. “Great Scott you’re 88! That’s some serious s---, love you! 😎,” Fox, 65, captioned an Instagram post , which featured a photo of the duo having dinner.
“Today I turn 88…I’ve seen some serious s---,” Christopher wrote that day on X . “The most serious of it all is love. I love my family, my friends, and my wonderful fans. The power of love remains.”
Of course, Lloyd has thoughts on getting older, as he tells PEOPLE. “I want to get a script with another part that I feel I can fulfill. That’s what I’ve always wanted, and it’s never ceased.”
He quips, “So I worry a little bit that there might be a great role for me, old fart guy, but they decide, ‘No, no, not Lloyd. He’s 88. He’s liable to drop dead on the set.’”
